summary: Sprint retrospective: Architecture established the stdlib contract; database delivered the constrained schema; backend implemented validated CRUD; frontend integrated the three-column board; QA added and passed lifecycle coverage while noting the failed-save dialog UX gap; security verified input, SQL, rendering, and static-path safeguards; manager coordinated the completed handoffs.
decisions: Retrospective dialogue: Architect: “I set a dependency-free HTTP, SQLite, and vanilla-JS contract that the implementation followed.” Database: “I delivered the tasks schema and status constraint that unblocked the API.” Backend: “I added validated CRUD and task movement endpoints using parameterized SQLite values.” Frontend: “The board now creates, edits, moves, and deletes tasks through the completed API.” QA: “The lifecycle regression test passed; I also found that an edit dialog closes after a failed save.” Security: “Input limits, validation, SQL parameterization, textContent rendering, and static-path containment all checked out.” Manager: “The planned handoffs completed without blockers; the only follow-up recorded was QA’s minor edit-dialog UX observation.”
